title: Applied AI Engineer
description: About Monte Carlo Monte Carlo is the agent trust platform that autonomously observes, fixes, and continuously improves agents and the data that powers them — so enterprises can scale trust at the speed of AI. Bayes, our AI teammate, does the work: detecting, triaging, troubleshooting, and fixing issues in AI agents and the data powering them. The result is self-improving agents that get better with every fix instead of drifting. More than 400 enterprises, including Amazon, PepsiCo, CNN, Nasdaq, and JetBlue, rely on Monte Carlo. Learn more at montecarlo.ai. The Role We're building the products that tell enterprises whether their AI agents can be trusted — and we need someone who works end to end, from an ambiguous problem statement through research, prototyping, and production. You'd get the problem, not the spec: research the approaches, prototype, prove what works, build it, and integrate it into the platform alongside our engineering and data science teams. This role exists because agent observability moved from roadmap to revenue faster than anyone predicted, and the work is now on the critical path. What You'll Do Take an open problem end-to-end — from research and prototyping through production, killing what doesn't work before it becomes someone's roadmap Design and ship agent-powered features — root-cause analysis, incident triage, monitor generation — and integrate them into the platform with our engineering team Build the eval infrastructure that makes those features safe to change: golden datasets, regression suites, offline and online scoring, and the judgment calls about what "good" means Own retrieval and context pipelines over customer metadata, lineage, and query history, and instrument agent behavior in production — traces, failure taxonomies, cost and latency budgets — to close the loop on quality Partner with data science on detection quality and experiment design, and with PM on what an agent should do versus what it merely can do Set the technical bar for how we build with LLMs — patterns, guardrails, and the internal tooling other engineers reuse What We're Looking For You've built agents in production with real users. Not integrated a framework. Not worked on a team that had one. Built them — agents with real autonomy and internal loops, where the model uses tools and decides what to do next without a human in the middle, and you kept them running once real users showed up. RAG with a wrapper doesn't count. Neither does a set of MCP tools point at an API. You've run evals and monitored agents after launch. Agents are non-deterministic, so normal tests don't work on them. You've owned an eval framework — golden datasets, regression suites, offline and online scoring — not a folder of one-off scripts. And you've watched agents in production, not just in dev. Python, plus an ML or data science background. Python is your daily language and you're solid on the backend, though you don't need to be a distributed systems specialist.

title: Regisseur VPT
description: Binnen het Volledig Pakket Thuis(VPT)‑team in Woerden ondersteun je cliënten om zo lang mogelijk op een veilige en prettige manier thuis te blijven wonen. Opstellen, evalueren en bijstellen van zorgplannen in samenwerking met cliënten en hun naasten. Regie voeren bij complexe zorgsituaties, met name rondom cliënten met dementie. Afstemmen met huisartsen, behandelaren, wijkteams en andere ketenpartners. Begeleiden en ondersteunen van collega’s en bijdragen aan een goede samenwerking binnen het team. Wat je van ons mag verwachten Salaris volgens cao VVT, FWG 50: € 3.592 - € 4.822 (o.b.v. 36 uur). Direct een vast contract voor 24 tot 32 uur per week. Reiskostenvergoeding, 8% vakantietoeslag en 8,33% eindejaarsuitkering. Mogelijkheid om gebruik te maken van het meerkeuzesysteem, zoals extra verlof of een fietsregeling. Toegang tot o.a. HeyCoach, budgetcoach en DigiCoach voor jouw ontwikkeling. Bij Careyn krijg je meer dan de arbeidsvoorwaarden uit de cao VVT. Meer weten? Bekijk onze arbeidsvoorwaarden. Wat jij meebrengt Een diploma Verpleegkunde op mbo‑ of hbo‑niveau. Ervaring in de wijkverpleging en kennis van coördinatie van zorg. Leiderschap en het vermogen om overzicht te bewaren in complexe situaties. Sterke communicatieve vaardigheden en een verbindende werkstijl. Zelfstandigheid, organisatiesensitiviteit en het vermogen om prioriteiten te stellen. Over het team Je komt terecht in een betrokken VPT‑team van ongeveer 15 collega’s. De sfeer binnen het team is collegiaal en praktisch; collega's weten elkaar te vinden en werken samen aan passende zorg voor cliënten thuis. Binnen deze rol krijg je veel ruimte om zelfstandig te werken en richting te geven aan de verdere ontwikkeling van het team. Om de veiligheid van onze cliënten en medewerkers te waarborgen, is voor alle medewerkers die bij Careyn in dienst komen een Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag (VOG) vereist. description: At Forbes Advisor, our mission is to help readers turn their aspirations into reality. We arm people with trusted advice and guidance so they can make informed decisions they feel confident in and get back to doing the things they care about most. We are an experienced team of industry experts dedicated to helping readers make smart decisions and choose the right products with ease. Forbes Advisor boasts decades of experience across dozens of geographies and teams, including Content, SEO, Business Intelligence, Finance, HR, Marketing, Production, Technology and Sales. The team brings rich industry knowledge to Forbes Advisor's global coverage of consumer credit, debt, health, home improvement, banking, investing, credit cards, small business, education, insurance, loans, real estate and travel. We pair journalism with original research: every “best of” list we publish sits on a dataset our own team has collected, scored and can defend line by line. The Data Research and Product Testing teams own that evidence base. We decide what gets measured, how it gets weighted, and whether a claim survives scrutiny. It is the difference between an opinion piece and a recommendation a reader can act on. About the Role We want to stop writing “the manufacturer claims”. This role is the person who actually opens it, uses it for six weeks and finds out. You will run hands-on testing of physical products from your own home testing space. Products arrive, you test them against a written protocol, you log what happened, and your scores go straight into the rankings readers see. For Health categories you will also run the lab pipeline, sending samples out for third-party analysis and bringing the results back in. This is a role for someone already deep in the health space, not someone who intends to learn it on the way. We expect you to use AI in your day-to-day work to increase your output without compromising testing rigour. You should understand which AI techniques suit each task, put them into practice and demonstrate how they help you deliver more or work faster. Knowing what AI could do is not enough: using it effectively and checking the results is part of the role. What you'll do Run hands-on tests to a written protocol and record the results in a structured, comparable form. The output is a dataset, not an opinion. Help design those protocols: decide what to measure, how to measure it repeatably, and what would make a result invalid. Own the sample pipeline for your categories: sourcing, receipt, logging, retention, return and disposal. Document testing as you go, including photography and video, so the editorial team can show readers the work rather than assert it. Feed test scores into the Data Research scoring models, and flag loudly when a hands-on result contradicts what the spec sheet claims. Re-test on a defined cadence so published verdicts do not quietly go stale as products and plans change. Write findings up clearly enough for an editor to build

title: Engineering Manager
description: Meet Siena Siena is the Agent of Record for CX, built for consumer brands like Spanx, FIGS, Brooklinen, and Grüns. It runs as a connected multi-agent stack on top of a shared intelligence layer: agents that sell, support, listen, handle social and voice across the entire customer journey, turning every conversation into signal you can act on. The team We are a small, fully distributed, global team. We have built leverage into how we work, which is what lets a team this size move at the speed we do. We hire athletes. Everyone here owns real outcomes, defaults to writing over meetings, communicates with directness, and acts the moment they see something worth acting on. Low ego, high standards, fast clock. If you want to set the bar rather than follow one, keep reading. The Role Siena's engineering team is small, senior and AI-native, and it ships across several products at once. This role leads a large part of that team, as a partner to engineering leadership, and owns how it scales. You will own delivery, hiring and team health for your part, and make sure a fast-moving team keeps shipping well across areas that look nothing alike. This is a hands-on leadership seat with a senior team and a lot of firefighting, not a layer of process. What You'll Do You will lead a large part of the engineering team, owning their delivery, priorities and growth. You will own hiring and planning for your part of the team, and keep raising the bar. You will turn shifting priorities into a plan the team can execute, and make trade-offs visible to leadership. You will own problems wherever they land, switching from a security issue to a customer call to a technical design in the same day. You will run on-call and incident response for your areas, and step in technically when the team needs it. You will work with engineers and with teams across the company to find the better approach together, and make the call when one is needed. Who You Are The Bar: If you're missing any of these, this isn't the role for you. You have managed software engineers directly. You have owned hiring and planning for a team, and kept the bar high as the team grew. You have taken over a team you did not build and made it better. You have owned problems across unlike areas at once: technical, security and customer-facing. Strong Signal: Not dealbreakers, but what separates a good hire from a great one. You have low ego: you don't arrive with the answer, you work it out with the team, and you defend a view when it matters. Your technical depth is still live: you can still ship code, drive an incident and use coding agents yourself. You have made hard people calls (feedback, performance plans, promotions) and can walk through one. You cut and rebalance scope as new needs come in, without losing the plot. You have worked in an early-stage environment and delivered a result with little resource. Nice to Have: Bonus, not required. You bring a security-first approach to how a team builds and ships.
